Theorem
[Weakened no local collapsing] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0134 ↗ def:chow-iii-reduced-volume-strong-collapse ↗ thm:chow-iii-reduced-volume-monotonicity 1. ch19:19.51–19.52\group Reduced Geometry

There is $c_1(n)\le 1/2$ such that strong $\kappa $-collapse at scale $r$ implies \[ \widetilde V_*(\varepsilon r^2)\le \frac{e^{n(n-1)/6}}{(4\pi )^{n/2}}\varepsilon ^{n/2} +\omega _{n-1}(n-2)^{(n-2)/2}e^{-(n-2)/2}e^{-1/(2\sqrt\varepsilon )}, \quad \varepsilon =\kappa ^{1/n}. \] If initial balls have a uniform volume lower bound, the flow is weakly $\kappa $-noncollapsed at all points and scales before the final half-time, with $\kappa $ depending only on the stated geometric data.
